clue.text: Diets require little money

definitions.meaning: diets are the means by which people get slim, read whimsically as ways of becoming thin
a small income, barely enough to live on

explanation.surface: Slimming plans cost hardly anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'require' is only a link between the two definitions; the first one is whimsical, reading the phrase literally as the way to get thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Diets are ways to get thin, and the phrase also means a meagre income, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Italian ladies inscribe their names on metal

parts.note: to sign is to write your name on something
ore is the rock that metal is mined from, a common crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: Women in Italy engrave their names on a sheet of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the plural of the Italian form of address for a married woman, here used for the women themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian word for a married woman, and its plural is used for women in general.

clue.text: She fell in love with Rochester Court ages ago

definitions.text: She fell in love with Rochester
definitions.meaning: the governess heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel loves Mr Rochester
a circuit court of travelling judges in medieval England

explanation.surface: A woman fell for a man named Rochester and they courted long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a verb about wooing, but it is a noun: the medieval circuit court held by travelling judges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë heroine is a governess who loves her employer, and the same word names a medieval travelling assize court.

clue.text: Where the drunken mugger may be incarcerated for battery

definitions.text: Where the drunken mugger may be incarcerated
definitions.meaning: a police cell where a drunk is left to sober up, read as a cell for drying out
an electrical cell with paste rather than liquid electrolyte

explanation.surface: A drunk who attacked someone may be locked up for assault and battery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' looks like the crime of assault, but it is the electrical sense; 'for' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell for drying out a drunk is a joke reading; the real sense is a non-liquid electric battery like a torch cell.

clue.text: Reports that we claim to possess spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
what we say belongs to us is described as ours

explanation.surface: Stories claim that we own some liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports here means hearsay or gossip passed around, unconfirmed stories.

clue.text: Another nest containing a bird

indicators.note: the words Another nest hold a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A second nest has a bird in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join of 'anothER NEst'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: County people support Norman Short

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath and holds up the first
the name Norman is cut short, losing its second half

parts.note: taken as written before cutting
folk means people

explanation.surface: Locals back a small man called Norman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman Short' reads like a person's name, but Short is an instruction to clip Norman to NOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county on the east coast of East Anglia.

clue.text: Scrooge fit to feature in less famous French novel

indicators.note: the words before are to appear inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge is the archetypal skinflint
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A Dickens miser is good enough to appear in a lesser-known French book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less famous' looks like one phrase, but 'less' is the container and 'famous' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo's celebrated novel, set in nineteenth-century France.

clue.text: A father daren't deal out unlawful punishment

indicators.note: dealing out cards mixes up their order, so these letters are spread around afresh

explanation.surface: A dad hesitates to dole out illegal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal out' looks like administering the punishment, but it rearranges A FATHER DARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating someone in tar and feathers was a mob punishment carried out without any legal process.

clue.text: Man leaves a German to enter cathedral city with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the trimmed phrase goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

indicators.note: the word Man departs from the phrase that follows

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks out on a German woman to go into a city with a cathedral eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man leaves' removes MAN from A GERMAN, leaving AGER, which goes into ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly and with relish is doing it eagerly; the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Subordinate accountant from a Spanish island

parts.note: minor means lesser or subordinate
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A junior accountant comes from Spain's islands.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: It's open to discussion when a thousand return as well

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for as well is read backwards

parts.note: too means as well

explanation.surface: Something is still up for debate when a thousand people come back too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; the definition is an adjective, as in a moot point, not the noun for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one still debatable and unresolved.

clue.text: The type of news provided by America

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or news
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: This is the kind of news supplied by the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology it is a rank of classification, a kind or class of organism.

clue.text: Summary given by Colorado attorney

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado
DA is a district attorney, the US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A Colorado lawyer gives a closing summing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A concluding passage that rounds off a piece, loosely a closing recap.

clue.text: Call upon Violet not to stand

parts.note: Vi is the usual short form of the name Violet
the opposite of standing is to sit

explanation.surface: A visitor asks Violet to stay seated.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a visit at home.

clue.text: Commonplace exhortation to prohibit trainee driver

parts.note: the command to prohibit is the imperative ban
a trainee driver is a learner, abbreviated to L from the L-plate, here with the article A in front

explanation.surface: Someone urges a ban on learner drivers, which is a dull idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole wordplay reads as a slogan, 'Ban a learner!', with L the British learner-driver plate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite and unoriginal, ordinary to the point of dullness.

clue.text: Distinguished policeman

definitions.meaning: out of the ordinary, marked out from others
a ... constable, a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: An eminent police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a special constable, a volunteer officer, is known informally by the adjective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptional things are marked out from others, and a British volunteer constable is known by the same word.

clue.text: Son spoke of being followed

parts.note: talked means spoke

explanation.surface: A son talked about being tailed by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stealthily tracked or pursued is being followed.

clue.text: Agent is not to do the decorating again

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: The agent refuses to redecorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying fresh coats of paint is redecorating, a second round of decorating work.

clue.text: I'll eat my hat!

parts.note: read literally: something both edible and a style of hat, a flat-crowned brim style named after a meat pastry

explanation.surface: An expression of total disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation of disbelief is read literally: the food is also a flat-topped hat, so the hat can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat with a flat crown is named after the British meat pastry it resembles, so it can be both eaten and worn.

clue.text: Nestor disturbed about a breach of faith

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter
disturbed letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The wise old Greek Nestor is upset about a betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges NESTOR into TRESON; 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest disloyalty, a betrayal of trust.

clue.text: Blackberry bush encountered in leisurely walk by the rail, way

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway, split here as rail and way
an amble is a slow, relaxed stroll

explanation.surface: A thorny bush met on a stroll beside the railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway; 'encountered in' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorny shrub that bears blackberries.

clue.text: Artillery brass hats

definitions.meaning: senior military officers, high-ranking important people

explanation.surface: Cannons and top-ranking officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy weapons are large guns, and the same phrase is slang for powerful senior figures.

clue.text: He plunders equipment held by the orchestra

indicators.note: the equipment word is enclosed within the musical group

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
rig means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A thief's tools are kept by the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or outlaw who robs travellers is a plunderer.

clue.text: Put up with a pain in the neck!

explanation.surface: Tolerating an irritating person.
explanation.definitionFit: Endured is the past tense of bear, and the same word means a tedious person.

clue.text: Block the Western border

parts.note: edge means border or margin

explanation.surface: Barricade the western frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapered chunk of wood or metal used to hold a door is a block.

clue.text: Lean over and pay attention

definitions.meaning: a ship heeling or tilting to one side

explanation.surface: Bend down and listen carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship tilts to one side, and the same old word means to hear or heed.

clue.text: Male politician in possession of cannabis

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A male MP is caught holding marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the hemp plant, grown for fibre and the drug.

clue.text: English monk of current importance in Spain

parts.note: Bro is short for Brother, the title of a monk

explanation.surface: An English monk is topical in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like topical, but it means a river's flow: a river of importance in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river of northern Spain, flowing to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Daily train

definitions.meaning: a British daily newspaper with this name
a fast train stopping at few stations

explanation.surface: A train every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A national British newspaper bears the name, as does a fast rail service with few stops.

clue.text: Hesitation to note anger and resentment

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitating
B is a musical note
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Faltering over a note leads to fury and bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence is feeling aggrieved, a sense of being slighted.

clue.text: Adhere to agreement, and don't disarm completely

definitions.meaning: hold on to a single blade, read whimsically as retaining one weapon

explanation.surface: Stick to the deal and don't lay down every weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase differently, keep one sword: retain a single blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Honouring a promise is fulfilling it; split differently, the phrase means holding on to a single blade.
